# testdata/baseline

A throwaway ed25519 key pair and a detached signature, generated by the real
`ssh-keygen` (OpenSSH_10.4p1) on 2026-08-06 for tests.

- `testkey`, `testkey.pub` — **test key. Not a release key, not trusted by
  anything, deliberately committed in the clear.** Real release and baseline
  signing keys are generated by a human, held offline (2-of-3, hardware) and
  never touch this repository or any test. That boundary is the seam: nothing in
  this tree generates, stores or requests a production signing key.
- `message.json` — canonical bytes (sorted keys, no floats; the timestamp is a
  `baseline.Seconds` decimal string).
- `message.json.sig` — `ssh-keygen -Y sign -n manifest.aurvet.dev`, i.e. produced
  by OpenSSH and not by this package.

Two jobs. First, key and signature parsing keeps coverage on a machine with no
`ssh-keygen` installed, where the interop tests skip. Second, `message.json.sig`
is a **golden**: ed25519 is deterministic and nothing in the signing path reads a
clock, so `baseline.Sign` over `message.json` must reproduce these exact bytes.
If that assertion ever fails, the wire format changed and every signature already
in a chain just became unverifiable — which is precisely the kind of change that
must not pass silently.
